INTRO.welcome.subtitle: Your personal finance manager
INTRO.welcome.footer: By logging in you agree to the Privacy Policy and the Terms of Use of the application
INTRO.offline.descr.title: OFFLINE ACCOUNT:
INTRO.offline.descr: Your data will only be stored on your device, and will be safe as long as you don't uninstall the app or change phone. To prevent data loss, it is recommended to make a backup regularly from the app settings.
INTRO.sl1Descr: Your default currency will be used in reports and general charts. You will be able to change the currency and the app language later at any time in the application settings
INTRO.sl2Descr: Your data is only yours. We store the information directly on your device, without going through external servers. This makes it possible to use the app even without internet
INTRO.sl2Descr2: Also, the source code of the application is public, anyone can collaborate on it and see how it works
INTRO.lastSlideDescr: With Monekin, you can finally achieve the financial independence you want so much. You will have graphs, budgets, tips, statistics and much more about your money.
INTRO.lastSlideDescr2: We hope you enjoy your experience! Do not hesitate to contact us in case of doubts, suggestions...

descr.insufficient_data: It looks like we don't have enough expenses to calculate your financial health. Add some expenses/incomes in this period to allow us to help you!
descr.very_good: Congratulations! Your financial health is tremendous. We hope you continue your good streak and continue learning with Monekin
descr.good: Great! Your financial health is good. Visit the analysis tab to see how to save even more!

monthsWithoutIncome.title: Survival rate
monthsWithoutIncome.subtitle: Given your balance, amount of time you could go without income
monthsWithoutIncome.text.zero: You couldn't survive a month without income at this rate of expenses!
monthsWithoutIncome.text.one: You could barely survive approximately a month without income at this rate of expenses!
monthsWithoutIncome.text.other: You could survive approximately {{ n }} months without income at this rate of spending.
monthsWithoutIncome.text.infinite: You could survive approximately all your life without income at this rate of spending.
monthsWithoutIncome.suggestion: Remember that it is advisable to always keep this ratio above 5 months at least. If you see that you do not have a sufficient savings cushion, reduce unnecessary expenses.
monthsWithoutIncome.insufficient_data: It looks like we don't have enough expenses to calculate how many months you could survive without income. Enter a few transactions and come back here to check your financial health
monthsWithoutIncome.formula: Money available in your accounts ÷ your average monthly expenses in this period.
monthsWithoutIncome.unlock: Record at least 4 transactions, some of them expenses, within this period.

savingsPercentage.title: Savings percentage
savingsPercentage.subtitle: What part of your income is not spent in this period

text.good: Congratulations! You have managed to save {{value}}% of your income during this period. It seems that you are already an expert, keep up the good work!
text.normal: Congratulations, you have managed to save {{value}}% of your income during this period.
text.bad: You have managed to save {{value}}% of your income during this period. However, we think you can still do much more!
text.very_bad: Wow, you haven't managed to save anything during this period.

savingsPercentage.suggestion: Remember that it is advisable to save at least 15-20% of what you earn.
savingsPercentage.formula: (Income − expenses) ÷ income, all within the selected range.
savingsPercentage.insufficient_data: There is not enough activity in this period to judge how much of your money you keep.
savingsPercentage.unlock: Record one income within this period, or at least 10 transactions of any kind.

debtToAssetRatio.title: Debt-to-asset ratio
debtToAssetRatio.subtitle: How much of what you own is offset by outstanding debt

text.value: Your outstanding debt is {{value}}% of your gross assets.
text.no_assets: You have outstanding debt but no recorded assets to back it.

debtToAssetRatio.suggestion: A lower ratio generally means you are better able to cover your debts with what you own.
debtToAssetRatio.insufficient_data: You are not tracking any debt or asset yet, so there is no balance sheet to judge.
debtToAssetRatio.formula: Outstanding debt ÷ gross assets, both as of the end of the selected range.
debtToAssetRatio.unlock: Add one of your debts or one of your assets (a house, a car...).

cashFlowConsistency.title: Cash-flow consistency
cashFlowConsistency.subtitle: How much of this period you kept your spending within your income

text.good: You spent within your means during {{value}}% of this period. Your cash flow is steady.
text.normal: You spent within your means during {{value}}% of this period.
text.bad: You only spent within your means during {{value}}% of this period, so your cash flow swings a lot.

cashFlowConsistency.suggestion: Spreading the big payments and keeping a similar pace all along makes your finances far more predictable.
cashFlowConsistency.insufficient_data: There is not enough activity spread along this range to tell how steady your cash flow is.
cashFlowConsistency.formula: We split the range into several parts and share out your income between them. In each part, spending at most what falls to you counts in full, spending twice as much counts as nothing, and in between counts proportionally.
cashFlowConsistency.unlock: Pick a range with activity in at least 3 of its parts.

investmentRatio.title: Investment ratio
investmentRatio.subtitle: What part of your income you put into securities in this period

text.value: You put {{value}}% of your income into securities during this period.
text.none: You haven't put any money into securities during this period.

investmentRatio.suggestion: Investing part of your income regularly helps your money grow faster than inflation.
investmentRatio.build_emergency_fund: Prioritize your emergency fund first. Each month of runway, up to five, progressively unlocks the points earned by your investment ratio.
investmentRatio.runway_insufficient_data: We can't score this ratio until your emergency runway can be measured.
investmentRatio.formula: Gross security purchases and positive cost-basis increases recorded in portfolio snapshots ÷ income, all within the selected range.
investmentRatio.insufficient_data: You had no investment account open during this period, so we can't measure this part of your finances.
investmentRatio.unlock: Open an investment account, or pick a range in which one of them was already open.
investmentRatio.runway_unlock: Pick a range with at least 4 transactions and some recorded expenses so your emergency runway can be measured.

howCalculated.intro: Your score blends these 5 indicators, each with its own weight. When there isn't enough data for one of them yet, its weight is shared proportionally among the rest, so your score can still reach 100.

composition.earnedDescr: Points you have already won with the data of this range.
composition.pendingDescr: What you are still missing in the indicators we can measure today.
composition.pausedDescr: {{indicators}}: you don't use them yet, so we cannot measure their points.
composition.scoreExplanation: Your score ({{score}}) only takes into account the {{measurable}} points we can measure today, so the ones we cannot measure are not dragging it down.

FINANCIAL-HEALTH.lowReliability: This score leans on {{measurable}} of the {{total}} indicators only, so take it as a first sketch: the more of them you use, the closer it will get to your reality.
FINANCIAL-HEALTH.shortRange: A range shorter than a month leaves out paydays and bills, which distorts indicators such as your savings rate. Widen it for a steadier score.
FINANCIAL-HEALTH.noComparisonNote: This app is yours and yours only: we never compare you with other users, we compare you with yourself.

MANUAL-IMPORT.title: Manual import
MANUAL-IMPORT.descr: Import transactions from a .csv file manually
steps-descr: Select a .csv file from your device. Make sure it has a first row that describes the name of each column.
Select the column where the value of each transaction is specified. Use negative values for expenses and positive values for income.

Select the column where the account to which each transaction belongs is specified. You can also select a default account in case we cannot find the account you want. If a default account is not specified, we will create one with the same name.
Specify the column where the transaction category name is located. You must specify a default category so that we assign this category to transactions, in case the category cannot be found.
Specify the column where the transaction tags are located. If not specified, transactions will be created with default tags.
Select the column where the date of each transaction is specified. If not specified, transactions will be created with the current date.
Specifies the columns for other optional transaction attributes.
